newsitem.title: UK: UK gas output leads rise in energy production - DTI.
newsitem.headline: UK gas output leads rise in energy production - DTI.

text.p: Gas production in Britain helped push total energy output in the three months to January 1997 to 82.5 million tonnes of oil equivalent, up 7.0 percent over the corresponding period the previous year, Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) figures showed.

The DTI, in its latest statistical report on energy output and consumption, said production of natural gas, oil and primary electricity rose by 13.4 percent, 5.0 percent and 9.2 percent respectively, while production of coal fell by 5.1 percent.

Total energy consumption rose 2.3 percent during the same period to 66.6 million tonnes of oil equivalent. Consumption of natural gas increased 7.7 percent and petroleum products by 1.8 percent, while coal consumption fell 10.9 percent.
Total use of petroleum, including non-energy use, in the three months November 1996-January 1997, was 21.4 million tonnes, 1.5 percent higher than in the corresponding period a year earlier, it said.
